key_insight: A deterministic multi-agent workflow can reduce unsafe medical AI failures by forcing complete symptom collection and screening for high-uncertainty outputs before diagnosis is handed off.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve the reliability of patient-facing diagnostic assistants by lowering the risk of premature conclusions and undetected hallucinations.
method: Enforce OLDCARTS symptom completeness with a neuro-symbolic state-tracking gate before any diagnostic step.
Compute semantic entropy from 5 independent diagnostic samples to flag divergent or uncertain outputs.
Use deterministic orchestration instead of LLM-as-a-judge routing to control handoffs.
evidence_signal: In 150 simulated test cases, the full system reached 49.3% diagnostic precision, an 11.3-point absolute gain over the unconstrained baseline, and OLDCARTS completeness was negatively correlated with semantic entropy (r = -0.181, p < 0.05).
watch_item: Results come from simulated patients and one model setup, so real-world clinical performance, generalizability, and workflow integration still need validation.
paper_title: Agentic AI-based Framework for Mitigating Premature Diagnostic Handoff and Silent Hallucination in Healthcare Applications
